## Findings
- claim-1: The two Theorem 5.4 families are \(\{s_\mu: i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) and \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-6@L18-L33|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: For \(i=j=p=2,c=5\), task 132’s exact integral Pieri/Smith computation establishes \(J_{2,5}/\Lambda_+J_{2,5}\cong\mathbb Z^6\), torsion-free. [artifact 189fc5f912d5ce0d7f385f5f68873379380542c3b14807b48344196febd2a397]
- claim-3: Here \(r=7,q=4,n=11\), hence \(a=\min(p,c)=2\), \(b=2\), and \(N=\binom{a+b}{a}=6\). The accepted generating families specialize to \[ \mathcal F_{\rm top}=\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\}, \quad \mathcal F_{\rm bot}=\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}. \] Since either accepted six-element family generates \(J_{2,5}\), its images surject \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow J_{2,5}/\Lambda_+J_{2,5}\cong\mathbb Z^6\). This surjection is unimodular, so the images are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis. A proper subfamily cannot generate the quotient and therefore cannot generate \(J_{2,5}\). Thus both families are minimal generating sets.
## Strategy
For \(r=7,q=4,n=11\), \(a=\min(p,c)=2\), \(b=2\), hence \(N=\binom{4}{2}=6\). The accepted generation result gives the two generating families
\[
\mathcal F_{\rm top}=\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{42},s_{33},s_{43},s_{44}\},
\quad
\mathcal F_{\rm bot}=\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{222},s_{2211},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}.
\]
Task 132 gives \(J_{2,5}/\Lambda_+J_{2,5}\cong\mathbb Z^6\), torsion-free. Thus either generating family induces a surjection \(\mathbb Z^6\twoheadrightarrow\mathbb Z^6\), hence an isomorphism by the indexed-family Nakayama criterion. Its images are a basis of indecomposables.

Any generating set of \(J_{2,5}\) surjects onto \(\mathbb Z^6\), so has at least six elements. Therefore both displayed six-element families are minimum-cardinality and irredundant generating sets.

The requested \(i=j=p=2,\ c=5\) minimality corollary is established relative to the accepted project inputs.

## Gaps
The conclusion depends on task 132’s accepted finite computation and the accepted generation result; it is not an all-parameter statement or an independently source-backed general theorem.
